description.purpose: Search across GitHub issues and pull requests by free-text query and return ranked smart IDs.
when_to_use: When the user wants to find an issue or PR by partial title, body keyword, or label.
When the exact issue/PR number is unknown.
limitations: Returns at most 30 results per call (GitHub API page size).
Search index lag of up to 60s for newly created items.
No code search included — use the GitHub web UI for code-text matches.
description.parameter_overview: Single `query` string supporting GitHub search qualifiers (e.g. `is:open author:alice`); ranked results returned as smart IDs of the form gh-prod-github:object:Issue:owner/repo#42.

query.description: Free-text search query, optionally with GitHub qualifiers.

truncation.guidance_template: Showing {N} of {Total} matches. Refine with GitHub qualifiers (e.g., `is:open`, `author:`) or use `cursor` to paginate.

description.purpose: Fetch the full GitHub object addressed by a smart ID (Issue, PullRequest, or Release).
when_to_use: When you have a smart ID returned by `search` or `list_objects`.
When the full object payload is required (e.g., body, comments, mergeability).
limitations: Returns full object including potentially large body markdown — consider `properties` projection.
404 if the object was deleted; PRs converted from issues retain their number.
description.parameter_overview: Single `id` string in the smart-ID format `gh-prod-github:object:{Issue|PullRequest|Release}:{owner/repo#number}` for issues/PRs or `:rel_id` for Releases.

truncation.guidance_template: Object exceeded {threshold} tokens; {N} fields included. Re-call with `properties: ['title','state']` to project.

description.purpose: List the available top-level GitHub object collections (Issue, PullRequest, Release) for discovery.
when_to_use: At session start to discover what data the GitHub MCP exposes.
When mapping a user request to the right object type.
limitations: Returns metadata only — use `list_objects` to enumerate within a collection.
description.parameter_overview: Optional `pattern` (glob) and `include_schema` (bool); defaults return all collections without schema.

description.purpose: List GitHub objects within a chosen collection with filter, sort, projection, and pagination.
when_to_use: When enumerating issues or PRs of a repo.
When a server-side filter (state=open) or sort (created desc) is needed.
limitations: GitHub list endpoints require a repo context (`owner` + `repo`); pass via filter.
Max 100 records per call.
Filter expressions limited to GitHub's documented filter qualifiers.

truncation.guidance_template: Returned {N} of approximately {Total} {collection}. Use `cursor` to paginate or `properties: ['title','state']` to project fewer fields.

description.purpose: Create a new GitHub Issue/PullRequest/Release or update an existing one (smart routing by id presence).
when_to_use: When opening a new Issue or PR.
When editing an Issue's title/body/state.
limitations: Releases cannot be updated by tag — only by id; supply id for updates.
PR creation requires `head` and `base` branches; both must exist.
Re-creating a release with the same tag fails with 422.
description.parameter_overview: `collection` selects type. `data` alone creates; `id` + `data` updates. For PR creation `data.head`/`data.base` required.

truncation.guidance_template: {action} succeeded for {collection} #{number}. Refetch with `properties` projection if response truncated.

description.purpose: Delete a GitHub Release (Issues and PRs cannot be deleted via API; close them instead).
when_to_use: When removing a draft release.
When cleaning up test releases on a sandbox repo.
when_not_to_use: For Issues — call `issues_close` instead (GitHub does not support issue deletion via REST).
limitations: Only Release supports delete; attempting Issue/PR delete returns 405.
Once deleted, the release is gone; tag remains.
`confirm: true` is mandatory.
description.parameter_overview: `type: 'object'` + `id` (smart ID of Release) + `confirm: true`. Batch delete supported via `ids` array.

truncation.guidance_template: Deleted {deleted_count} of {requested}. Re-call with remaining IDs; idempotent.

description.purpose: Close an open GitHub Issue (idempotent — re-closing a closed issue is a no-op).
when_to_use: When a fix is shipped and the bug Issue should auto-close.
When rejecting a feature request.
limitations: Re-closing a closed Issue returns the same closed object (idempotent).
Closing a locked Issue requires admin permissions.
description.parameter_overview: Required `id` (smart ID of Issue). Optional `state_reason` enum (`completed`, `not_planned`, `reopened`).

description.purpose: Merge an open GitHub Pull Request using the requested merge strategy.
when_to_use: When required reviews and CI checks have passed and the PR should land.
When applying a squash or rebase merge programmatically.
limitations: Already-merged PR returns 405 (not idempotent in GitHub semantics).
Branch protection rules can block merge with 405.
Closed-without-merge PRs cannot be merged — must be reopened first.
description.parameter_overview: Required `id` (smart ID of PullRequest). Optional `merge_method` (`merge`/`squash`/`rebase`, default `merge`) and `commit_title`/`commit_message`.

description.purpose: Create a new GitHub Release tied to a git tag (drafts and prereleases supported).
when_to_use: When automating a release pipeline (CI tagged a build).
When publishing release notes for a new version.
limitations: Re-creating a release with the same tag returns 422 (NOT idempotent).
Tag must already exist OR `target_commitish` must be supplied for tag creation.
Body markdown is rendered server-side; max 125,000 chars.
description.parameter_overview: Required `tag_name`. Optional `name` (release title), `body` (notes), `draft` (default false), `prerelease` (default false), `target_commitish` (commit/branch to tag).

description.purpose: Create a pull request from a branch in two coordinated steps: verify branch ref exists, then open the PR.
when_to_use: When the agent has just pushed a branch and wants to open a PR in the same turn.
When the branch existence is uncertain (e.g., across forks).
limitations: Two-step workflow — partial failure leaves branch verified but PR uncreated; safe to retry.
Requires `head` branch to exist before invocation.
Cross-fork PRs need fully-qualified `head` (e.g., `username:branch`).
description.parameter_overview: Required `owner`, `repo`, `head_branch`, `base_branch`, `title`. Optional `body` (markdown). Coarse parameters representing user intent — internal step IDs are hidden.
